answer_1.quote: We first collect 270 real world questions from Youtube videos and answers from domain experts... to tackle this problem further, we adopt a data-centric approach where we create a synthetic dataset... We benchmark our dataset across 6 state of the art MLLMs...
answer_1.outputs: Long-form textual answers to student questions about video lectures

answer_2.quote: We show results using BLEU-1, ROUGE-L and METEOR. We also evaluate using a semantic metric, Entailment Score (ES), and LLM-based FactQA Precision and Recall metrics... We also design a set of new metrics based on the Qualitative Preference Study...

answer_3.quote: We then use GPT-4o to obtain the scores. For the scores for which both human annotators agreed... we get scores from GPT and find the Cohen's Kappa to be 0.7162... This shows moderate to high agreement between GPT-4o scores and human annotations.

answer_4.quote: We have 2 student annotators (graduates) to annotate the quality scores according to the Likert Scale... We provided 10 university students with 5 random questions... Students selected their preferred answer and listed the qualities influencing their choice.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated generated answers using a Likert scale for Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking, and Using Pedagogical Techniques; separate preference study asked students to choose the better answer and indicate preferred qualities.
